decisions.reason: The decision removes level shifting only for sensor interfaces; the LED interface has separate power and logic-level requirements that remain unchanged.
Removing sensor logic-level shifting does not change which power rails are monitored or the INA3221 monitoring topology.
The standalone USB supply must still power the same 3.3V rail and sensors; the sensor level-shifter decision does not alter its regulator or source-selection requirements.
The DCDC1 output and system-rail regulation remain unchanged by removal of sensor-interface level shifting.
The source decision concerns sensor logic interfaces and has no effect on the passive buzzer selection or interface.
The client explicitly establishes that the 5V-powered SPS30 is 3.3V-logic compatible and therefore requires no sensor-board level shifter.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The level shifter was listed as DNP (Do Not Populate) by default — just the footprint on the PCB without components soldered. The purpose was future-proofing: if someone later connects a 5V-logic sensor to the spare I2C0 or UART connectors, they could populate the BSS138s to make it work. Since all sensors in our current BOM work at 3.3V (including SPS30 and ZE08 which are 5V-powered but 3.3V logic compatible), the level shifter is not needed for any connected sensor. You can skip it entirely to save board space. If we ever need 5V-logic sensors later, we'll add a small adapter board rather than reserving permanent footprints.

decisions.reason: The source preserves the existing sensor and spare connectors while removing separate level-shifter circuitry; the connector inventory and fanout role remain unchanged.
The removed BSS138 logic-level shifter is distinct from the retained I2C pull-ups and optional series resistors, whose values and topology are unaffected.
The decision applies to sensor-interface level shifting and does not change the LED daughterboard's part, package, count, or form.
A possible future adapter board is contingent rather than a current project board, so the four-board topology remains unchanged.
Sensor logic-level shifting does not affect the panel-control connector inventory or on-board BOOT-button policy.
The client confirms that SPS30 and ZE08 remain 5V-powered; only their logic compatibility is clarified, so the switchable 5V rail and its powered loads remain unchanged.
